title: European Parliament committee adopts draft resolution on COP31 priorities
excerpt: The Environment Committee voted 50 to 16 to support a faster fossil fuel phase-out and increased climate finance ahead of the November conference in Antalya.
bodyHtml:
The Committee on the Environment, Climate and Food Safety of the European Parliament adopted a draft resolution on October 1, 2026, outlining priorities for the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) scheduled for 9-20 November in Antalya, Türkiye. The committee approved the text by 50 votes to 16 with 3 abstentions.

The resolution calls for an accelerated transition away from fossil fuels and an increase in climate finance for vulnerable countries. MEPs urged the European Union to lead negotiations toward a fossil fuel non-proliferation treaty and requested time-bound plans to phase out fossil fuel subsidies and production. The committee also noted that preliminary data shows EU emissions rose by 1% between 2024 and 2025.

The full European Parliament is scheduled to vote on the final resolution during its 19-22 October plenary session. A delegation of 15 MEPs, headed by Lídia Pereira, will attend the climate talks from 16 to 20 November.

The committee also called for the rapid scaling-up of predictable and accessible finance for the fund for responding to loss and damage, and for all parties to deliver on the goal of tripling adaptation finance by 2035.
